title: permission-catalog-and-evidence-export-draft
content:
Purpose
This working doc captures the proposed permission catalog, the attribute-first entitlement model for RBAC v2, the audit/event schema for SIEM exports, and an evidence-automation pipeline to produce compliant artifacts for audits. Intended audience: security, platform, SRE, product, and engineering owners involved in the RBAC v2 rollout.

Scope
- Define canonical permission catalog (resource x action x purpose) and canonical entitlement attributes.
- Specify audit event schema and SIEM export formats (JSON and CEF mapping).
- Propose evidence artifact generation, retention, and automation pipeline.
- Provide phased rollout and migration approach from RBAC v1 (role-based) to RBAC v2 (attribute-anchored).

Executive summary (TL;DR)
We propose a hybrid-ABAC model where principals are assigned attribute sets (team, org_unit, trust_level, environment, project_id) and policies are defined as predicates over these attributes plus resource tags. The permission catalog will be the source of truth for UI/console ACLs and for the policy-evaluation service. Audit events will include a minimal tenancy and decision trace so SIEM can reconstruct who got what access and why. Evidence artifacts (signed attestations + replayable audit shards) will be generated automatically at key lifecycle events (grant, revoke, policy change, emergency escalation) and pushed to a hardened evidence-store for 7 years by default.

Design principles
- Developer-friendly: APIs and SDKs use the same permission names as the console.
- Low-latency policy checks: cache stable attributes and precompile frequent policy shapes.
- Deterministic audit: every policy decision emits a structured event with enough context to replay a decision.
- Cryptographic integrity for evidence: HMAC-signed manifests with KMS-backed keys.
- Gradual migration: route a percentage of requests to v2 policy evaluation in canary.

Permission catalog (proposed canonical format)
- Each permission entry: permission_id, short_name, description, resource_pattern, allowed_actions, sensitivity_label, example_use_cases, deprecated_by (optional), owners.
- Example entry (text):
  permission_id: perm.project.read
  short_name: project.read
  description: Read project metadata and user-facing configuration
  resource_pattern: projects/{project_id}
  allowed_actions: [read, list]
  sensitivity_label: low
  example_use_cases: UI project list, telemetry aggregation
  owners: product-projects

Attribute model (principal and resource attributes)
- Principal attributes: principal_id, type (user/service), teams, org_unit, roles_legacy (for migration mapping), trust_level (low/standard/high), credential_type (password, key, short_lived_token), enrolled_2fa, manager_id, contract_type (fte/ contractor/partner)
- Resource attributes: resource_id, resource_type, project_id, environment (prod/stage/dev), sensitivity, owner_team, creation_ts, tags
- Policy predicate example: allow if principal.teams contains resource.owner_team AND principal.trust_level >= required_trust_level AND resource.environment != 'prod' OR hasApprovalTicket==true

Policy evaluation flow
1) Request arrives at API gateway with auth token.
2) Auth service mints validated principal assertion (JWT with minimal attributes).
3) Policy engine fetches resource attributes (cache first) and evaluates policy predicate.
4) Decision returns allow/deny + decision_id and list of matched_rules; engine emits audit event with decision trace.

Audit event schema (canonical JSON fields)
- event_id: uuid
- event_ts: ISO8601 UTC
- service: string (e.g., authz-engine)
- request_id: uuid (gateway correlation id)
- principal: {principal_id: string, principal_type: string, attributes_snapshot_id: string}
- resource: {resource_type: string, resource_id: string}
- action: string (e.g., project.read)
- decision: allow | deny | error
- matched_rules: [string] (list of rule ids or names)
- decision_trace: string (short textual explanation or pointer to rule tree)
- policy_version: string
- cache_hit: boolean
- reason_code: string (high level reason for decision)
- evidence_id: string (id pointing to stored evidence artifact, if created)
- signer_kid: string (KMS key id used if signing an evidence manifest)

Notes: In the JSON above the principal and resource sub-objects are flattened for SIEM export (see SIEM export mapping below). We must keep each top-level field stable; new fields appended should use a namespaced prefix to avoid breaks.

SIEM export formats and mapping
- Two export paths needed: (A) near-real-time (ELT) JSON stream to our log cluster and (B) syslog/CEF formatted messages for legacy SIEMs.
- JSON ELT: emit the full canonical audit event as JSON to log-producer topic (kafka.redwood.audit.v2). Use gzip + newline-delimited JSON for transport.
- CEF mapping example (single-line):
  CEF:0|Redwood|AuthZ|1.0|decision:${decision}|${action}|${severity}|rt=${event_ts} suser=${principal_id} src=${principal_type} cs1Label=resource cs1=${resource_type}:${resource_id} flexString1=${matched_rules}
- Field mapping table (abridged):
  event_id -> event_id
  event_ts -> rt or timestamp
  principal.principal_id -> suser
  principal.principal_type -> src
  resource -> cs1
  action -> msg
  decision -> outcome (allowed/denied)
  matched_rules -> flexString1
  policy_version -> cs2
  evidence_id -> externalId

SIEM consumer filters and dashboards (recommendations)
- Splunk sample: index=redwood_audit source=audit_v2 decision=deny | stats count by action, principal_type, resource_type
- Alert rules: repeated deny for same principal within 5m across different resources -> potential compromised token; decision changed from allow to deny after policy change -> flag for regression testing.

Evidence artifact model
- Artifact types: decision-manifest (signed JSON snapshot of the decision and inputs), policy-change-attestation (signed policy bundle + who/when), access-grant-evidence (approval ticket + signed grant), replay-shard (compressed audit events for a time slice).
- Manifest fields: evidence_id, produced_ts, decision_id, producer_service, input_hash (sha256 of attributes+resource+policy), signed_by_kid, signature, storage_path, retention_policy.
- Signing: use KMS asymmetric signing (ECDSA P-256 or RSA-2048), store signer KID in manifest. The verification tool will pull public keys from KMS cache.

Evidence automation pipeline (overview)
- Trigger points: policy-decision events marked with evidence_required=true, policy bundle publishes, manual attestations, periodic snapshots (daily mirror of last-24h decisions).
- Orchestration: lightweight workflow service (step functions / temporal) runs steps: collect_events -> generate_manifest -> sign_manifest -> push_to_store -> index_metadata -> notify_compliance
- Storage: write manifests and shards to evidence-bucket/encrypted (SSE-KMS) with lifecycle rules (7y cold storage). Add checksum files and replication to a geo-redundant backup.
- Indexing: metadata pushed to evidence-index (Elasticsearch) with fields: evidence_id, decision_ids, time_range, owners, policy_version, tags, retention_expiry.
- Access control: evidence-bucket read restricted via bucket-level policies; evidence-index access limited to compliance and delegated auditors.
- Tamper detection: weekly ledger job that computes Merkle roots over manifests and writes root hash to an immutable ledger service (append-only log).

Migration and rollout plan (phases)
- Phase 0: Preparatory (2 weeks)
  - Finalize permission catalog draft, owners assigned, create test projects for pilot.
  - Implement canonical audit fields in a feature branch.
- Phase 1: Pilot (4 weeks)
  - Pick 2 internal services and 3 stable customer tenants. Enable policy engine v2 in logging-only mode (emit decision_v2 but do not enforce). Collect discrepancies.
  - Run fuzzy matcher to map legacy roles -> attribute combinations and build migration map.
- Phase 2: Shadow (6 weeks)
  - Enable decision_v2 enforcement for traffic percentage (10% -> 50%) with automatic rollback on SLO regressions. Create canary dashboards.
  - Evidence automation enabled for all v2 decisions in pilot tenants.
- Phase 3: Staged rollout (8–12 weeks)
  - Expand to org-wide teams by org_unit with preflight checks (no denied-critical requests in last 48h).
  - Migration migration-tool available (one-click map + preview + dry-run apply).
- Phase 4: Enterprise sweep + hard cutover (4 weeks)
  - Final migration window, deprecate legacy enforcement API, full enforcement by default.

Gating criteria / success metrics
- Decision mismatch rate (v1 vs v2) < 0.5% for 7 consecutive days during shadow.
- No customer-facing SLO degradation attributable to authz changes.
- Evidence artifact generation success rate > 99.5%.
- SIEM events delivered within 30s 95th percentile.

Operational runbooks (high level)
- Rollback: set authz-gateway.flag.rbac_v2_enforce=false and clear v2 tokens cache (ttl 30s) -> results propagate within 60s.
- Evidence rescan: orchestration supports rescan(range) to regenerate shards for a time period; flagged for manual approve.
- Audit request: compliance can retrieve evidence by evidence_id using evidence-cli with ephemeral presigned link.

Security considerations
- KMS rotation: signer keys rotated yearly; old keys retained for verification only; manifests include signer_kid.
- Minimization: only include attributes necessary for policy evaluation and logging; PII flags must be redacted before evidence export.
- Emergency access: emergency_bypass role creates special evidence entries flagged and requires follow-up attestations (3rd party reviewer).

Open questions / decisions needed
- Canonical severity mapping: how to compute severity value in CEF for each action? (owner: product-security)
- Evidence retention defaults: 7y vs 3y for contractors (legal to decide).
- Approval ticket linkage: we need a small schema for linking external ITSM URLs and storing minimal hash vs full text.
- Should we support per-tenant custom attributes? impacts caching and policy-size explosion.

Next steps / short checklist
- [ ] Align on final permission catalog and owners (owners assigned in this doc).
- [ ] Implement audit_event canonical fields in authz-engine (PR ready: github:pull/redwood/infra/487).
- [ ] Stand up evidence-bucket + indexing pipeline in dev.
- [ ] Run pilot with two internal services (owners: Ravi Patel, Elena García).
- [ ] Schedule cross-functional review with legal for retention and evidence export policies.

Appendix: sample audit event (newline-delimited JSON example)

  \"event_id\": \"c1a2f8d2-5e3a-4a91-b2d9-7b2f7c5a9d3e\",
  \"event_ts\": \"2025-09-30T17:14:22Z\",
  \"service\": \"authz-engine\",
  \"request_id\": \"req-7f6d2a9b\",
  \"principal_id\": \"u:maya.chen@redwood.com\",
  \"principal_type\": \"user\",
  \"attributes_snapshot_id\": \"snap-20250930-1714\",
  \"resource_type\": \"projects\",
  \"resource_id\": \"projects/p-12345\",
  \"action\": \"project.read\",
  \"decision\": \"allow\",
  \"matched_rules\": \"rule-58,rule-61\",
  \"decision_trace\": \"team-match + trust_level OK\",
  \"policy_version\": \"v2-2025-09-01\",
  \"cache_hit\": \"true\",
  \"reason_code\": \"match_owner_team\",
  \"evidence_id\": \"evid-20250930-0001\",
  \"signer_kid\": \"kms://projects/redwood/keys/authz-sign-2024\"
}
